title: Agents in Business Central – part 1 – the architecture
summary: Agents in Business Central 27.4 allow you to create custom agents that process tasks asynchronously using an orchestrator architecture. The post explains how agents are triggered via task creation, how the orchestrator manages execution with separate sessions and transactions, and how to handle incoming and outgoing messages programmatically.
key_points: Custom agents (public preview since 27.4) need the Custom Agent capability enabled, the AGENT - ADMIN permission set, a 27.4+ sandbox and billing setup in the tenant
Agents start working when a task is created with the Agent Task Builder codeunit; the Agent Task codeunit can restart, stop or check the status of tasks
The orchestrator runs tasks asynchronously and in parallel, each in its own session and transaction with the agent as user
Incoming emails can be handled by a Job Queue codeunit that uses the email conversation ID to add replies to an existing task via Agent Task Message Builder, including attachments
Outgoing messages are found by output type and reviewed status, processed, and then marked as Sent with the Agent Message codeunit

quotes.text: Since Business Central 27.4 minor update you can create your own agents inside Business Central.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes when custom agents became available and marks the beginning of the feature capability

quotes.text: Each task can be seen as a separate user session, thus uncommitted data may not be viewable and concurrent modifications can collide.
quotes.why_it_matters: Important architectural consideration for developers implementing agent tasks to avoid data consistency issues
